items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The helper `_filter_prefetch_queryset` reads clearly. Names such as `predicate`, `low_mark`, `high_mark` and `window` say what they hold, and formatting matches the module. It has no comment on the window-function trick, which is a minor gap on non-obvious logic.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One short private helper is shared by the reverse-FK and M2M paths. It reuses existing ORM pieces (Window, RowNumber, GreaterThan/LessThanOrEqual, clear_limits, get_order_by) and leaves the filter guard untouched. The temp test file was removed and no dead code is left.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It checks `supports_over_clause` and raises a specific `NotSupportedError` with a clear message. It handles `high_mark is None`, defaults the db with `DEFAULT_DB_ALIAS`, and swallows no errors.

items.name: Per-parent slice semantics for open/bounded slices
items.name_zh: 开放/有界切片按父对象分区
items.evidence: It filters per parent in SQL with `Window(RowNumber(), partition_by=field_name, ...)`, using `GreaterThan(window, low_mark)` plus `LessThanOrEqual` only when `high_mark` is set. `clear_limits()` runs on the copy made by `.using()`, so the user's queryset is not mutated.
